definitions.gloss: to do one's best, to try hard
definitions.explanation: To make a strong effort, to work hard toward a goal. One of the most commonly used words of encouragement in Japanese.

definitions.gloss: to persevere, to hang in there
definitions.explanation: To persist despite difficulties, to not give up.

examples.japanese: {頑張|がんば}って⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧！
⟦{辛|つら}くて→辛い：01112_tsurai⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{頑張|がんば}り⟦{続|つづ}けた→続ける：01231_tsuzukeru⟧。
examples.english: I kept going even though it was tough.

examples.japanese: ⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧{頑張|がんば}れば⟦{終|お}わる→終わる：00567_owaru⟧。
examples.english: If you push a little more, you'll finish.

examples.japanese: ⟦{試験|しけん}→試験：01422_shiken⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{頑張|がんば}って⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: I'm working hard for the exam.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦{遅|おそ}く→遅い：00533_osoi⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧{頑張|がんば}って⟦{勉強|べんきょう}している→勉強する：00527_benkyousuru⟧。
examples.english: She studies hard late every day.

examples.japanese: ⟦{何度|なんど}→何度：17592_nando⟧⟦{失敗|しっぱい}して→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{諦|あきら}めず→諦める：01813_akirameru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{頑張|がんば}った⟦{結果|けっか}→結果：02486_kekka⟧、⟦やっと→やっと：01561_yatto⟧⟦{合格|ごうかく}→合格：02816_goukaku⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: After persevering without giving up despite failing many times, I finally passed.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: ⟦{自動詞|じどうし}→自動詞：10977_jidoushi⟧ (intransitive). Pattern: {頑張|がんば}る (try hard) / X⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{頑張|がんば}る (work hard at X—less common).

ASPECT: て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ indicates ongoing effort. {頑張|がんば}って⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ = 'is working hard' or 'has been trying hard.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {頑張|がんば}って！ (Good luck! Hang in there!)
- {頑張|がんば}って⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧ (Please do your best—polite)
- {頑張|がんば}ります (I'll do my best)
- {頑張|がんば}れ！ (Go for it!—imperative, casual)
- ⟦もっと→もっと：00798_motto⟧{頑張|がんば}る (try harder)

CULTURAL NOTE: {頑張|がんば}って is one of the most common expressions of encouragement in Japanese. It's used in a wide variety of situations—before exams, during sports, at work, etc. However, be careful using it with someone who is already struggling or exhausted, as it might add pressure.

REGISTER: Neutral. The expression {頑張|がんば}って can feel casual while {頑張|がんば}って⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧ is polite.
